title: Tissue Engineering of the Intestine in a Murine Model
protocol: Sterilize dissection instruments by autoclave.
Euthanize the donor mouse according to local IACUC protocols.
Make a midline incision to gain access to the peritoneal cavity.
Reflect skin flaps as needed to improve exposure.
Eviscerate the small bowel and divide it just distal to the ligament of Treitz.
Separate the small bowel from its mesentery using sharp and gentle blunt dissection.
Identify the ileocecal junction and divide the small bowel 5 mm proximal to this.
Open the intestine lengthwise along the antimesenteric border in a Petri dish with 10 ml 4 °C, sterile Hanks' buffered saline (HBSS) / 1X antibiotic-antifungal (Anti-Anti) solution.
Clear fecal matter from the opened intestine with gentle agitation.
Transfer the opened intestine to a 15ml centrifuge tube with 10 ml of 4 °C, sterile HBSS / 1X anti-anti.
Wash the opened intestine three times in 10 ml of 4 ° C, sterile HBSS / 1X anti-anti in a test tube.
Discard floating material, which is mesenchymal debris after each wash.
Remove the washing solution carefully with a pipet.
Mince the washed intestine in a Petri dish with 10 ml of 4 °C sterile HBSS / 1X anti-anti to less than 1 mm square pieces using scissors.
Gather the minced material up with an automatic pipette and place it into a test tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 500 rpm for 8 min.
Discard the supernatant, which contains fat and mesenchyme.
Weigh out 5 mg of dispase, 142 mg of collagenase type 1, and add sterile HBSS up to a volume of 40 ml to prepare the digestion solution.
Incubate the minced, washed material with the digestion solution at 37 °C for 20 min.
Retrieve the test tube and further disrupt the digested tissue by trituration with a 10 ml pipette between 20 to 50 times until a uniform appearance is obtained.
Centrifuge the test tube for 5 min at 800 rpm.
Discard the supernatant, which contains single cells.
Stop the digestion reaction with 10 ml of 4 °C sterile Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) plus 10% v/v heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (HI-FBS).
Resuspend the pellet and shake the tube.
Centrifuge the test tube for 5 min at 800 rpm.
Remove the supernatant carefully with an automatic pipet until the last few drops.
Use a disposable plastic pipet for the last few drops to avoid resuspending the pellet.
Trim the distal 2 mm of a disposable 1,000 microliter pipet tip with scissors prepared with 70% ethanol in distilled water.
Place the scaffold into a 4-well culture plate.
Load the organoid units onto the scaffold with the 1,000 microliter pipet, first into the lumen and then onto the outer surface.
Use a forceps to ensure coating of the lumen.
Do not disrupt or break open the cylindrical shape of the polymer.
Use a syngeneic host mouse on the same background as the donor if available.
Otherwise, employ an immunocompromised nonobese diabetic/severe combined immunodeficient (NOD/SCID) animal.
Induce general anesthesia with isoflurane.
Shave the mouse's abdomen.
Prep and drape the mouse's abdomen.
Make a 5 mm midline incision to gain entrance to the peritoneal cavity.
Identify and carefully eviscerate the greater omentum.
Place the loaded polymer onto the omentum and wrap it with the tissue.
Do not tear the omentum.
Secure the polymer to the omentum with a 5-0 monocryl suture.
Gently replace the omentum with the wrapped polymer into its anatomic position.
Close the abdominal incision in layers using 4-0 vicryl sutures.
Run the muscle closure and take care not to injure the abdominal viscera below the incision.
Use interrupted sutures for the skin.
Administer postoperative analgesia with 2 mg/kg ketoprofen in sterile water as a subcutaneous wheal adjacent to the incision.
Evaluate the animal daily for signs of pain or distress.
If pain or distress is observed on post-operative day 2, administer an additional dose of ketoprofen.
By the third postoperative day, ensure the animal is fully recovered without evidence of pain or distress.
Allow the mouse to recuperate and the tissue-engineered intestine to grow for four weeks.
Give the animal ad libitum access to rodent chow and water with Septra 200 mg / 40 mg per 5 ml at a 1:100 dilution.
Humanely euthanize the host animal four weeks after implantation.
Reopen the original incision and reflect the skin cephalad to facilitate access to the peritoneal cavity.
Open the muscle layer and identify the tissue-engineered construct as a globe of tissue.
Take down adhesions to the construct from intraabdominal viscera using sharp dissection.
Fix the construct in formalin for later paraffin mounting or use fresh for biochemical assays such as real-time PCR or protein isolation.
